evidence: Concrete path: graph posts a durable transcript request to a present summarizer (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32-34; DESIGN-NOTES.md:250,258); its helper stalls without a completion report (DESIGN-NOTES.md:248,251,256); graph therefore leaves the request pending and discoverable (DESIGN-NOTES.md:256-257). The demonstration stops there: the approved contract requires durable requests, explicit completion, and recovery after occupant loss, but states no deadline or automatic stall detection for a still-present occupant. The notes place dispatch/reply behavior in role instructions and reject a plugin worker pool (DESIGN-NOTES.md:248-250,258); CURRENT-DESIGN.md:54 explicitly leaves crash/retry behavior for further design. Thus indefinite pending work is a real operational risk, but this story does not reach a contradiction of a stated transcript-workflow guarantee. It would require an additional liveness requirement to confirm this finding.
